# A third chapter repeating the second chapter's sort key

The contested term once more, sorted the way the chapter before it sorted it.
A rival key repeated in a further chapter is not a further thing for the
author to fix, so it must draw no report of its own:
[Contested]{.index sort="Zzz"}.

A range opened here and never closed anywhere in the book: a one-chapter
fault this chapter's own never-closed report states, which the book's
cross-chapter report must NOT name — it has no counterpart in any other
chapter's record: [Unclosed]{.index range="open"}.

The closing whose opening was refused a chapter earlier. It keeps its own
locator, and the book must not name it either: the displaced opening named no
range end, so no counterpart is visible: [Spanned]{.index range="close"}.

The closing of the would-be pair opened a chapter earlier. Both halves are
unpaired — each chapter refuses its own — and this is the one shape the book's
report names, both marks of it. This book's marker is in its FIRST chapter, so
the report being drawn at all proves it is drawn by the last chapter in book
order — the one that has seen every record — rather than by the marker
chapter: [Bridged]{.index range="close"}.

A second opening for a term whose range is still open, inside ONE chapter of a
book: the chapter is the pairing scope, so its own already-open report must
fire here exactly as it does in a single document, and the first opening is
the one the closing pairs with: [Twice Opened]{.index range="open"} then
[Twice Opened]{.index range="open"}, closed by
[Twice Opened]{.index range="close"}.
